As Alexander advances into India, Takshashila submits to a truce while Chanakya secretly prepares for war. In the Paurav Kingdom, Prince Puru struggles to save the wounded King Bamani amid Kanishk’s betrayal and Queen Anusuya’s humiliation. With Bamani saved by Chanakya, Puru is torn between rescuing his mother and defending the nation. Defying storms and fate, Alexander vows to defeat Porus, unaware of India’s hidden strength—its war elephants—setting the stage for their inevitable clash.

Shivdutt humiliates Anusuya, who vows vengeance and foretells her son Puru’s return. Chanakya guides Porus, teaching strategy over force. As Alexander advances, Takshashila’s king plots betrayal, but Porus sets a close-range ambush, using war elephants to neutralize the cavalry. Loyalties are uncertain, yet Porus boldly signals the attack, routing Alexander’s forces while Chanakya withdraws to spare bloodshed.

Porus defies Alexander, vowing to protect his motherland despite Takshashila’s betrayal. Fire frightens his elephants, but he retreats strategically, luring the invader into a deadly trap. Faking his death by destroying the Jhelum bridge, Porus delays Alexander and turns the tide with cunning. Ambhiraj betrays India, yet Porus survives, revealing his masterstroke. Guided by Chanakya, he rises to reclaim Paurav, free his mother, and unite Bharat against Alexander’s dream.

Porus vows to reclaim the Paurav kingdom and punish Shiv Dutt for dishonoring his mother. During the spring festival, disguised women warriors infiltrate the celebrations. Though an explosion was meant to kill him, Porus secretly returns, signaling his survival. Shiv Dutt panics as Puru moves to rescue Queen Anusuya, while Chanakya warns patience over anger. Faking his death, Porus lures Shiv Dutt into overconfidence. Courtesans strike with poisoned veils, decimating his army. Facing Porus and his mother, Shiv Dutt realizes too late that his cruelty has sealed his fate.

Anusuya avenges her family by killing Shiv Dutt, exposing his betrayal and treason, while Puru secretly prepares for coronation to unite India against Alexander at Jhelum. Chaos erupts as Porus is hunted, Kanishk is imprisoned, and the bridge explosion confession surfaces. Chanakya’s intellect clashes with Alexander’s power, who now plots to crush Bharat. At the coronation, King Purushottam performs sacred rituals, turning the ceremony into a battlefield of honor and strategy. Unarmed but resolute, Porus stands ready to defend his motherland and fulfill his deadly vow against Alexander

Radha’s uncontrolled anguish and harsh words toward Krishna lead to a divine curse that banishes her from Golok. She is destined to be born in the mortal world, forgetting Krishna, Golok, and even herself for a hundred years. Krishna accepts this separation as part of a greater cosmic design, choosing to bear the pain of remembrance alone. He believes their separation will transform love into a path of spiritual awakening for humanity. In the mortal world of Barsana and Gokul, destiny slowly brings them closer again. Through longing, play, and unspoken bonds, their forgotten love begins to reawaken.

title: Dice Media

schedules.description: The episode centers on a visit from Anita’s boisterous, unfiltered parents—Akshata (Deepika Amin) and Kiran Sharma (Shishir Sharma). The quiet, disciplined, and currently somber Solanki household is suddenly upended by the high-energy Sharmas. The primary conflict arises when the two sets of parents have a "polite clash" over how to care for the ailing Kiran Solanki and, more pivotally, the couple's future plans regarding children.

With the house now fully "merged," Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) decide to throw a surprise anniversary party for the "Folks." While their intentions are pure, the episode explores how a "celebration" can quickly become a source of stress when dealing with a chronic illness and interfering relatives.

The episode revolves around a chaotic Sunday at the Solanki household. The central plot involves Kiran Solanki (Shishir Sharma) needing a hearing aid, but it quickly spirals into a larger commentary on how the family members are "deaf" to each other's actual needs and desires.

The finale moves away from the day-to-day bickering and centers on a quiet realization: Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita (Eisha Chopra) have finally stopped "adjusting" and have started living. The episode focuses on the family accepting their "New Normal" while acknowledging that the road ahead with Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) health will be challenging but shared.

The episode begins with Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita (Esha Chopra) gathering the family for a "serious talk." After months of private deliberation, they drop the ultimate truth bomb: they have decided to adopt a child instead of pursuing a biological pregnancy.

The episode centers on the Home Study, a critical step in the Indian adoption process where a government social worker visits the family to determine if they are fit to raise a child. However, the title "The Damaad Test" (The Son-in-law Test) refers to the parallel pressure Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) feels to prove he is a "good son" while also being a "good son-in-law" to Anita’s (Eisha Chopra) visiting parents.

While Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) are stuck in the agonizing "waiting period" of the CARA process, the tension shifts to the two sets of parents. The episode highlights that even when everyone agrees on the goal (the grandchild), their different ways of expressing love and anxiety can lead to a hilarious yet deep-seated cultural clash.

The wait is over: Anita and Nikhil are matched with a child. However, instead of the pure euphoria they expected, they are hit with a wave of intense anxiety. The title "Are We Ready?" reflects the internal crisis the couple faces as they realize their lives are about to change irrevocably—not in nine months, but in a matter of days.

The finale begins with the arrival of the moment Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) have spent the entire season preparing for: bringing their adopted daughter home. The episode isn't just about the new arrival, but about how each family member adapts to their "What The Future" role.
Shaurya struggles with getting recognition for his efforts at work while Sanya debates shifting out of her home. Both of them help each other step out of their comfort zones and grow
As Shaurya and Sanya shift in together, Sanya takes a gamble at work which impacts both of their lives.
As Shaurya and Sanya deal with the realization of having fallen for each other, they have to prioritize what is more important - emotions or logic?

Having finally admitted their feelings to each other, Shaurya and Sanya's honeymoon weekend is over and they must get back to reality. With Shaurya up for a promotion and Sanya doubtful about her growth in this company, what is this new couple in for?

With appraisals around the corner, Shaurya and Sanya brace themselves for the unexpected. Eventually, Shaurya gets his first real lesson in team management and Sanya makes a crucial decision to help her get what she wants.

To mark 3 months of being together, Shaurya convinces Sanya to organise something for their "monthiversary." However, things begin to get complicated as Shaurya finds himself working directly with Sanya - for the first time since they started dating.

Shaurya eventually ends up at Akhil’s party but to his surprise does not feel like he belongs there. Meanwhile, Ratna invites Sanya to have a drink with her. Sanya still upset about Shaurya lying to her begins to feel better with Ratna and her friends. To her surprise Shaurya shows up there as well to save their monthi-versary. However, things seem to go in the opposite direction soon.

Shaurya’s presentation does not go as planned and he ends up overpromising samples to the client on a three day deadline. This leads to the team having to work round the clock. Meanwhile, Sanya makes a plan to take a break from work and convinces Shaurya to do go somewhere together. Both Shaurya and Sanya finally spend some quality time with each other but things take a turn when Shaurya gets a call from Vinod.

Sanya decides to move back to her room. Shaurya isn’t happy about this. To make things worse Akhil is hard on him for overpromising and almost losing the client. Akhil demands that the team fixes the situation and gets them another chance.

The episode sets the stage for the series: Ray and Nikhat are best friends and roommates who have just started their journey into independent adulthood. The central conflict is the classic "End of the Month" crisis—where your bank account is empty, but your social and survival needs are not.

The episode centers on a surprise visit from Nikhat’s mother, which triggers a high-speed cleaning operation. For any young person living away from home, the "parental visit" is a performance of maturity, and Ray and Nikhat are determined to win an Oscar for "Most Responsible Adults."

The episode explores the gap between digital perception and reality. Ray and Nikhat find themselves caught in a cycle of comparing their "boring" lives to the filtered, high-glamour lives of their peers on Instagram.

The episode follows a high-stakes day for both girls. Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) is trying to climb the corporate ladder and has a critical presentation, while Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) is dealing with the thrill and anxiety of a potential romantic connection. The title reflects the constant "hustle" and the physical and metaphorical state of being "in transit" in life.

The episode is framed around a significant milestone: Nikhat’s (Aisha Ahmed) birthday. While birthdays are usually for celebrating, they often trigger a "Quarter-Life Crisis" where we compare our current reality to the versions of ourselves we imagined "then."

The episode revolves around the nightmare of moving houses in Mumbai. Ray and Nikhat are excited about their new "adult" space, but the transition from the old house to the new one becomes a comedy of errors that tests their patience and their friendship.

The episode explores the "Work-Life Balance" myth. Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed), now in a senior role with a fancy new apartment to pay for, is buried under deadlines, while Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) is trying to figure out how to be a "productive" freelancer without the structure of an office.

The episode centers on the loss of personal space. As Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) spend more time in their new apartment, the "honeymoon phase" of moving in ends. The title reflects the struggle to maintain one’s own identity ("Me") while being part of a co-dependent duo ("Us").

The episode centers on the arrival of Ray’s (Yashaswini Dayama) old school friend. Ray is excited to show off her "cool" Mumbai life, her "cool" roommate Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed), and her "cool" new apartment. However, the reunion doesn't go as planned, leading to a major case of "Social Comparison Anxiety."

Everything that could go wrong, does. The episode is a "comedy of errors" that quickly turns into an emotional crucible. As the girls juggle professional disasters and personal health scares, they are forced to answer the question: Are we just friends because it’s convenient, or are we family?

The episode picks up with Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) feeling the absolute peak of urban exhaustion. Between Nikhat’s soul-crushing corporate deadlines and Ray’s chaotic freelance schedule, they realize they are running on fumes. To blow off some steam before their planned trip home, they decide to have one last "epic" Mumbai night.

The episode follows Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) as they settle into their respective family homes. The initial "pampering phase" (where parents cook your favorite meals and do your laundry) ends abruptly, replaced by the suffocating routine and expectations they once ran away from.

While still in their respective hometowns, Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) encounter people from their past. The episode highlights the awkward friction that occurs when you realize your old friends have either stayed exactly the same or changed in ways you can no longer relate to.

The episode explores the complex, multi-generational layers of female relationships. It’s not just about the friendship between the two leads, but about the "sisterhood" they share with their mothers and the realization that their mothers were once young, ambitious, and confused women too.

The title "Out Of Office" is a play on their professional status, but it more accurately reflects their mental state. They’ve been "out of office" from their Mumbai lives for long enough to gain a new perspective. The episode focuses on the inevitable departure and the emotional weight of saying goodbye—this time with the maturity of adults who know exactly what they are going back to.

The episode opens with a camera crew following Neerav Kapoor (Nero) as he prepares for his day. Within the first five minutes, it becomes clear that Nero doesn't just want to be an actor; he believes he is already a legendary craftsman who simply hasn't been "discovered" yet.

The episode explores the concept of "Networking." Nero believes that his talent is so undeniable that if he can just get in front of the right person, the "tables will turn," and he will go from a nobody to a superstar. This leads him to infiltrate a high-profile industry event where he is, unsurprisingly, not fit.

Nero realizes that being a great actor isn't just about performing; it’s about observation and mentorship. He decides to take it upon himself to solve the "emotional blocks" of everyone around him, believing that his vast experience in playing fictional characters makes him an expert in real-world psychology.

Nero becomes obsessed with the idea that he is the perfect fit for a "desi" superhero franchise. He doesn't wait for a script or a casting call; he decides to live the life of a superhero to "absorb the essence" of the character. This leads to some of the most cringeworthy "public" moments in the entire series.

Nero becomes convinced that the secret to becoming a superstar lies in "Physical Functionality." He decides that his body needs to be a fine-tuned instrument capable of any physical feat, leading him to join a CrossFit-style gym. However, in true Nero fashion, he doesn't just work out—he turns the gym into a stage for his "performative athleticism."

Nero is faced with a harsh reality: his bank account is empty, and his "blockbuster" hasn't arrived. He decides to grace a small-scale, in-house corporate production with his "legendary" presence. He views this as a charitable act—a superstar helping out the common folk—but the corporate team views him as a total nightmare.

Nero decides that the mainstream industry is too "small-minded" to understand his vision. He takes on the role of Writer, Director, and Lead Actor to produce an avant-garde short film titled Reflections of Blood.

Nero realizes that "socially conscious" cinema is the current trend in the industry. He decides that to be a true "Hero," he needs to stand up for the marginalized. However, because it's Nero, he manages to turn a fight for "Equal Rights" into a self-centered campaign for "Actor’s Rights."

schedules.programName: High Is Well That Ends Well
schedules.description: The title is a classic Nero-ism—a mangled version of "All's Well That Ends Well," infused with his obsession with "vibrations" and high-frequency living. In this finale, Nero is faced with the ultimate test: a real, high-stakes opportunity that requires him to be... normal.

The documentary crew follows a rare moment of "crisis" in Nero’s life. His landlord has had enough of the "acting workshops" (noise) and unpaid dues. Nero, however, refuses to see this as a tragedy; he views it as the "Second Act" of his biopic where the hero hits rock bottom before the inevitable rise.

Arun (Vishal Vashishtha) is a former professional gamer, once known as "Flickshot," who left his passion to work a monotonous corporate job and support his family. When he sees his former teammate, Shekhar, succeeding on a massive stage, his suppressed passion resurfaces. Despite his father’s disapproval and the general stigma surrounding gaming as a career, Arun decides to quit his job and attempt a comeback.

Arun realizes he can’t win alone and begins the hunt for a new team. The episode focuses on the recruitment of a "misfit" squad:
Prachi: A badminton player struggling with an injury.
Jeetu: A delivery boy with natural, lightning-fast reflexes.
Adil: A young, tech-savvy enthusiast who acts as the team's initial bridge.
Raunak: A volatile but highly skilled "fragger." The task is harder than Arun anticipated, as he has to convince these individuals (and their skeptical families) that they have what it takes to be pros.99999999999

The team has assembled, but the chemistry is non-existent. Raunak’s ego clashes with the other members, and the group struggles to put their personal issues aside during practice. Arun has to step up not just as a player, but as a coach, to teach them that in Esports, individual brilliance is useless without team synergy. This episode highlights the "grind" of professional gaming and the steep learning curve.

With the tournament only a week away, the pressure reaches a boiling point. Arun’s father discovers he quit his job, leading to a major confrontation. Meanwhile, the team faces a crushing defeat in a practice match against established professionals, leaving their confidence shattered. However, seeing Arun's dedication eventually inspires his father to have a change of heart, and the team finally begins to gel as a unit.

The season finale takes place at the Indian Pro Gaming League. Team Clutch enters as the ultimate underdogs. After a shaky start and a brief internal conflict where Raunak almost walks out, the team reunites for a final stand. They reach a thrilling tie-breaker round where they must prove their worth. The series ends with the team securing a victory, using their prize money to chase their individual dreams while planning to build a permanent gaming headquarters.

We are introduced to Raviranjan, a small-town guy who balances life as a part-time YouTuber with his status as a "full-time" aspirant. While he acts confident (his rangbaaji), the episode reveals the underlying pressure he faces. He isn’t just seeking a job; he’s seeking the social status required to marry Jyoti. The episode sets up the stakes: it's a battle between his dreams and the harsh deadlines of the competitive exam world.

The reality check hits hard when the OSC results are announced and Ravi fails his first attempt. He faces taunts from his family and the crushing weight of societal judgment. Encouraged by Jyoti, who provides both emotional support and a strategic plan, Ravi moves from being a "casual" student to a "hardcore" aspirant. This episode highlights the physical and mental "grind" involved in the preparation.

As the wait for the next exam cycle continues, the "high" of hard work starts to fade into a "low" (Avroh means descent). Financial struggles, family tensions, and unexpected "villains" in the form of societal gatekeepers threaten to derail him. Ravi is forced to make difficult choices between his relationship with Jyoti and his focus on the exam, as the cracks in his mental health begin to show.

The finale focuses on the most agonizing part of the process: the wait. Ravi faces his final hurdles and a major internal crisis of self-doubt. The episode serves as a powerful commentary on the Indian examination system, exploring whether a job title truly defines a person's worth. It concludes Raviranjan's journey by showing how he manages to reclaim his self-respect (Swabhiman), regardless of the exam result.

The episode sets the stage for the ultimate "Generation Gap" social experiment. Akash (Rohan Shah) and Pooja (Aditi Myakal) are a modern married couple living in a spacious Mumbai apartment. However, their lifestyle is outpacing their income, leading them to a radical decision: renting out their spare rooms to bachelors.

After the initial adjustment period of the pilot, the household faces its first major logistical crisis—Food. The episode explores the chaos of shared groceries, differing diets, and the "disaster" that is a communal refrigerator.

After weeks of living together, the apartment has reached a state of "critical mess." Aashna (Kriti Vij), who takes pride in a clean and aesthetic home, finally snaps. The episode follows the couple's attempt to militarize the house cleaning process and the bachelors' hilariously lazy resistance.

The episode begins with a sense of impending change. After weeks of chaos, the experimental living arrangement—where a married couple (Akash and Pooja) shares their home with three bachelors (Rohit, Mohit, and Vishi)—is put to the test.

Maya, a Gen Z UX designer, joins Thoda Sukoon — a mental health startup with strict office hours, long workdays, and zero breathing space. Expecting flexibility and support, she instead finds herself caught in a whirlwind of deadlines and old-school hustle. As pressure mounts ahead of a major product launch and funding round, Maya connects with her burnt-out teammates. But when it comes to challenging the system — who’s willing to speak up?

Tight deadlines. Zero chill. And one very fed-up Maya. Maya’s ideas get ghosted, her dedication’s under the scanner, and the team? Busy minding their own burnout. Just when she finds a bit of empathy, things spiral again. Sleep is a myth, pressure is real, and Maya’s had enough. But when push comes to shove… does she stay, or finally hit CTRL+ALT+ESC?

Maya’s impulsive decision leaves her awkward around Chirag, who doesn’t miss a chance to tease her. As they open up about their generational views on work and life, Maya reaffirms her belief in mental health and Thoda Sukoon’s mission. But just as things start looking up, a bold move in a high-stakes meeting sparks serious tension with the higher-ups. Can Maya recover when her values put her at odds with the very system she’s trying to change?

While the team scrambles to fix minor app bugs, the real issues at Thoda Sukoon are swept under the rug — until it all explodes. An employee collapses from overwork, triggering a full-blown social media backlash. As tensions rise, Maya and Chirag are forced to face unresolved conflict, and the team must ask: how far is too far? Can this crisis spark real change in a toxic work culture, or is it already too late?

In the aftermath of Riddhi's collapse, Zooni spearheads a desperate negotiation for better working conditions. As a seemingly balanced work environment emerges, the team struggles to deliver, and blurred lines between professional and personal lives begin to fray. Are these simply growing pains for Thoda Sukoon, or are fresh, explosive complications on the horizon?

India’s fashion matriarch, Zahira, is making a bold move - bringing Zahiraan into the world of wearable luxury. But there’s a catch - neither she nor her team knows how to navigate this shift. Thus, comes in Ayesha - a rookie designer, a dreamer bursting with fresh ideas. But will she survive the cut-throat competition in fashion and at Zahiraan? Get ready for an intense drama, glamorous showdowns, and career-defining moments as the battle for success begins at Zahiraan.

Ayesha’s out-of-the-box ideas leave a mark on Zahira, but not everyone is impressed. As she tries to navigate the high-pressure world of fashion, her bold creativity ignites a war with her team. Amidst the chaos, an unexpected friendship with Sanchi gives Ayesha the confidence boost she desperately needs. But in an industry where talent isn’t enough, will this newfound support be her key to a major breakthrough?

The much-awaited Zahiraan launch is here, but disaster strikes! One unexpected error threatens to crumble Ayesha's hard-won validation from Zahira, and jeopardize both their careers. Meanwhile, Karan battles crippling self-doubt, wondering if he'll ever measure up to the perfection demanded by the high-stakes fashion world. Will their reputations survive?

Aditya and Prajakta are all set to tie the knot! As they navigate the excitement and chaos of wedding planning, a surprise guest from Prajakta's past arrives, turning their perfect day upside down. Will love triumph over unexpected challenges?
As Aditya and Prajakta celebrate their pre-wedding festivities, a shocking twist turns their world upside down! Will they handle the chaos together?
A perfect wedding, a hidden secret, and a love under threat. Will Aditya and Prajakta's love story survive the test of time?
As pre-wedding festivities unfold, Aditya stumbles upon a secret only Prajakta’s best friend knew. Can he handle the parts of her he’s just beginning to see?

The episode centers on the wedding of the lead couple, where everything seemingly goes wrong. However, instead of letting the chaos ruin the day, the couple realizes that the "imperfections" of their wedding reflect the reality of their relationship. They choose to embrace the mess, focusing on their commitment to each other.
The series introduces Nishant, Sakshi, and Huma as they begin their MBBS journey, adjusting to the demanding environment of medical college and forming new friendships.

A month into their studies, the trio struggles to balance an overwhelming syllabus, challenging practicals, and the desire to enjoy college life. An unexpected revelation about Nishant changes the group's dynamics.
Midterm results bring surprises, prompting celebrations that uncover deeper issues the friends must confront together.
Huma faces a crisis of confidence, seeking unconventional advice to regain her footing. A heartbreaking event forces the friends to reevaluate their priorities and the strength of their bond.
As final exams approach, Huma contemplates unethical shortcuts, leading to revelations that challenge perceptions and test the integrity of their friendship.

A month into their studies, the trio struggles to balance an overwhelming syllabus, challenging practicals, and the desire to enjoy college life. An unexpected revelation about Nishant changes the group's dynamics.

As final exams approach, Huma contemplates unethical shortcuts, leading to revelations that challenge perceptions and test the integrity of their friendship.
Dhruv and Kavya plan a lazy Sunday but feel the pressure of missing out when they see their friends enjoying exciting activities on social media. This leads them to seek ways to spice up their day.
A morning rush to work results in a tussle between Dhruv and Kavya, spoiling their moods. Throughout the day, they attempt to make amends, highlighting the irony and sweetness of their relationship.
A sleepless night due to mosquitoes leads to the discovery that Kavya's ex-boyfriend is getting married, prompting a long conversation about their past relationships.
Plans for a dinner at an Iranian restaurant get canceled, leading Dhruv and Kavya to attend a friend's house party. The night evolves into an unexpected adventure, ending at a local fair.
During a visit to a vineyard, Dhruv and Kavya open up about their insecurities and future aspirations, leading to deeper conversations about life and their relationship.

Kishore, an orphan has only one dream, to join the IndianArmy. When he gets thrown out of his orphanage, Masterji, an ex-army officer who left the army and is now working as a tailor, reluctantly adopts him. The khadoos Masterji and Kishore have only two things in common, their dream to serve the nation and their lonely lives. Will Masterji help Kishore achieve his own unfulfilled dreams to become a soldier, and will Kishore find a father in Masterji?

Captain Vikrant Sahay and his wife Vibha had a beautiful love story. But Vikrant’s sudden death in battle leaves the otherwise happy-go-lucky Vibha completely shocked. Unable to deal with Vikrant’s death, Vibha decides that the best way to honor him is to fulfill his dream, by joining the army herself, much against her family’s wishes. Will Vibha succeed and make her late husband, her family, and the country proud?

Tribhuvan, a dedicated Indian Army Officer comes across a young sweeper Tinku, who is a gifted shooter. Tribhuvan knows Tinku has a rare talent, and wants to enroll him in the shooting academy and then the Indian Army. However, owing to Tinku’s caste, his father is afraid of society’s taunts and is completely against this career choice. Will Tinku have the courage to fight back and rise above ‘log kya kahenge’?

Colonel Balram, a retired Indian Army Officer, returns home after several years of service, only to find himself completely disconnected from his son Aman. While Balram is failing at mending his relationship with Aman, he is also silently struggling with mental health issues, because of his days at war. Will Aman ever understand his father’s sacrifices for the country or will it be too late before he realises just how much his father loves him?

Veera’s martyred father’s last wish was for her to join the Indian armed forces. But Veera is not for it. The bravery and patriotism that the country remembers and celebrates him for, are the same things that took Veera’s father away from her. She’s been carrying this anger and hurt in her heart for too long, until she discovers a hidden letter.

Viraj and Arjun have been best friends since childhood. While Viraj loves his bachelor life and wants Arjun to move in as his flatmate, Arjun has other plans of ‘settling down’. What happens when this bachelor reveals he wants to be ‘unbachelored?’

The gang gets together to celebrate Arjun’s big news, but Viraj is concerned whether the dynamics of the group will change with its new addition. Will Khushi win over the gang and get Viraj's stamp of approval?

Its Arjun’s birthday, and Khushi steals the limelight with her unconventional celebration party. Tensions at the party rise when Viraj confronts Arjun about his change in behaviour since he started dating Khushi. Will Arjun pick pyaar or dosti?
The group tries to resolve tensions between Viraj and Arjun, but they both resist. As Viraj rants to Zara and Kaka about his friendships and relationships, he realises more about his true self.
The wedding day is here! Will Viraj stand by Arjun on the most important day of his life, and will he admit his true feelings to a special someone?

Shagun wants to keep the Filmy Weddings business floating and for that she’s willing to go to any lengths. Even if it means shooting a wedding film for Adhira’s ex-boyfriend – Akhil. Adhira is furious and tries her best to sabotage the entire project. Unfortunately, her one big hurdle is Dad, who has taken quite a fondness for Akhil. Check out the episode and find out what happens next!

Adhira and Shagun are in a disagreement about whom to select for a wedding film promo: a boring aunt from the bride's side or a lively drunk aunt from the groom's family. Things take a turn for the complicated when the parents also weigh in with their respective biases.

Vishnu, the Agarwal's househelp cum man friday is desired by the sisters as an office boy to help them sort out their business affairs. The parents are naturally opposed to the idea. Thus begins another standoff in the Agarwal household - and Vishnu's position in the house is at stake. Who will finally lay claim over Vishnu's priceless services?

In a footage from a wedding they just filmed, the sisters find a drunken confession from the bride's best friend. It turns out she is the groom's ex - and he hasn't told the bride to be. Caught in the moral dilemma of choosing to tell the bride or not, the sisters find themselves on other ends of the argument. Meanwhile, it is revealed that Adhira's father might have a similar secret hidden from everyone. Will the sisters do the morally right thing or the financially right thing? And what is the father's bizarre obsession with knowing who the groom's mom is?

Chasing a competitive business pitch to work for a coveted fashion firm, the sisters are again at different sides of a dilemma. The commitment to the new opportunity would be for a minimum two years, which Adhira is reluctant to make at the age of 25. Whereas Shagun, having already quit her high paying corporate job to join this business, sees no harm in seizing the opportunity with open arms. As their argument turns to a fight, we are left wondering if this is in fact the fight to end all fights. Will the sisters come to the same page and work for the pitch? Or will Happily Hitched disband for good?
Nikhil Solanki arrives at his in-laws' home, where a series of mishaps culminate in a significant blunder that upsets his father-in-law, Prakash Sharma. Both struggle to address the situation openly.
Prakash avoids acknowledging that Nikhil damaged his car, instead blaming neighborhood children. Nikhil's attempts to rectify the situation lead to further complications.
During Sudha and Prakash's anniversary celebration, relatives pose uncomfortable questions, challenging Nikhil's patience and composure.
A disagreement between Anita and her parents results in a cold war, leaving Nikhil caught between his wife and in-laws.
Nikhil expresses his feelings of being an outsider within the family, prompting an open discussion aimed at resolving underlying issues.

A few months after moving to Mumbai, Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita are finally settled. The peace is interrupted by the arrival of Nikhil's parents, Kiran (Shishir Sharma) and Vandana (Renuka Shahane), for a short visit. Anita, ever the perfectionist, is anxious to be the "perfect daughter-in-law," but her efforts are met with a series of awkward and hilarious hurdles.

The episode picks up with the fallout of Nikhil’s father, Kiran (Shishir Sharma), going missing during his walk in the previous episode. While he eventually returns, the tension doesn't dissipate. The "surprise" of the title is twofold: the unexpected arrival of Nikhil’s sister, Shreya (Kriti Vij), and the unsettling realization that something is physically or mentally "off" with Kiran.

The entire family—Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh), Anita (Eisha Chopra), Kiran (Shishir Sharma), Vandana (Renuka Shahane), and Shreya (Kriti Vij)—piles into a car to attend a relative's 60th birthday celebration. What was meant to be a joyful getaway becomes a pressure cooker for the long-standing resentment between the siblings.

The title is a poignant double entendre: it refers to a missing set of rings at the family function, but more deeply, it refers to the "missing" pieces of Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) memory. The facade of a "normal family vacation" finally crumbles, forcing the Solankis to stop pretending.

The title "House of Cards" refers to the fragile "perfect family" image the Solankis have tried to maintain. After the emotional explosion regarding Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) health and Shreya’s (Kriti Vij) marriage, the "house" has finally collapsed—but in its place, something more honest is being built.

In the Season 2 finale, "Home," Anita and Nikhil prepare to move into their own place. The episode resolves the season's friction between Anita and her mother-in-law, replacing awkward formalities with genuine mutual respect. As they move out, the story concludes that "home" isn't about physical space, but the emotional bridge built between two different generations.
The title "Circle of Life" refers to the poignant role reversal where the children now become the guardians of their parents, mirroring the care they once received.

The episode centers on a visit from Anita’s boisterous, unfiltered parents—Akshata (Deepika Amin) and Kiran Sharma (Shishir Sharma). The quiet, disciplined, and currently somber Solanki household is suddenly upended by the high-energy Sharmas. The primary conflict arises when the two sets of parents have a "polite clash" over how to care for the ailing Kiran Solanki and, more pivotally, the couple's future plans regarding children.

With the house now fully "merged," Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) decide to throw a surprise anniversary party for the "Folks." While their intentions are pure, the episode explores how a "celebration" can quickly become a source of stress when dealing with a chronic illness and interfering relatives.

The episode revolves around a chaotic Sunday at the Solanki household. The central plot involves Kiran Solanki (Shishir Sharma) needing a hearing aid, but it quickly spirals into a larger commentary on how the family members are "deaf" to each other's actual needs and desires.

The finale moves away from the day-to-day bickering and centers on a quiet realization: Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita (Eisha Chopra) have finally stopped "adjusting" and have started living. The episode focuses on the family accepting their "New Normal" while acknowledging that the road ahead with Kiran’s (Shishir Sharma) health will be challenging but shared.

The episode begins with Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) and Anita (Esha Chopra) gathering the family for a "serious talk." After months of private deliberation, they drop the ultimate truth bomb: they have decided to adopt a child instead of pursuing a biological pregnancy.

The episode centers on the Home Study, a critical step in the Indian adoption process where a government social worker visits the family to determine if they are fit to raise a child. However, the title "The Damaad Test" (The Son-in-law Test) refers to the parallel pressure Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) feels to prove he is a "good son" while also being a "good son-in-law" to Anita’s (Eisha Chopra) visiting parents.

While Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) are stuck in the agonizing "waiting period" of the CARA process, the tension shifts to the two sets of parents. The episode highlights that even when everyone agrees on the goal (the grandchild), their different ways of expressing love and anxiety can lead to a hilarious yet deep-seated cultural clash.

The wait is over: Anita and Nikhil are matched with a child. However, instead of the pure euphoria they expected, they are hit with a wave of intense anxiety. The title "Are We Ready?" reflects the internal crisis the couple faces as they realize their lives are about to change irrevocably—not in nine months, but in a matter of days.

The finale begins with the arrival of the moment Anita (Eisha Chopra) and Nikhil (Veer Rajwant Singh) have spent the entire season preparing for: bringing their adopted daughter home. The episode isn't just about the new arrival, but about how each family member adapts to their "What The Future" role.
Shaurya struggles with getting recognition for his efforts at work while Sanya debates shifting out of her home. Both of them help each other step out of their comfort zones and grow
As Shaurya and Sanya shift in together, Sanya takes a gamble at work which impacts both of their lives.
As Shaurya and Sanya deal with the realization of having fallen for each other, they have to prioritize what is more important - emotions or logic?

Having finally admitted their feelings to each other, Shaurya and Sanya's honeymoon weekend is over and they must get back to reality. With Shaurya up for a promotion and Sanya doubtful about her growth in this company, what is this new couple in for?

With appraisals around the corner, Shaurya and Sanya brace themselves for the unexpected. Eventually, Shaurya gets his first real lesson in team management and Sanya makes a crucial decision to help her get what she wants.

To mark 3 months of being together, Shaurya convinces Sanya to organise something for their "monthiversary." However, things begin to get complicated as Shaurya finds himself working directly with Sanya - for the first time since they started dating.

Shaurya eventually ends up at Akhil’s party but to his surprise does not feel like he belongs there. Meanwhile, Ratna invites Sanya to have a drink with her. Sanya still upset about Shaurya lying to her begins to feel better with Ratna and her friends. To her surprise Shaurya shows up there as well to save their monthi-versary. However, things seem to go in the opposite direction soon.

Shaurya’s presentation does not go as planned and he ends up overpromising samples to the client on a three day deadline. This leads to the team having to work round the clock. Meanwhile, Sanya makes a plan to take a break from work and convinces Shaurya to do go somewhere together. Both Shaurya and Sanya finally spend some quality time with each other but things take a turn when Shaurya gets a call from Vinod.

Sanya decides to move back to her room. Shaurya isn’t happy about this. To make things worse Akhil is hard on him for overpromising and almost losing the client. Akhil demands that the team fixes the situation and gets them another chance.

The episode sets the stage for the series: Ray and Nikhat are best friends and roommates who have just started their journey into independent adulthood. The central conflict is the classic "End of the Month" crisis—where your bank account is empty, but your social and survival needs are not.

The episode centers on a surprise visit from Nikhat’s mother, which triggers a high-speed cleaning operation. For any young person living away from home, the "parental visit" is a performance of maturity, and Ray and Nikhat are determined to win an Oscar for "Most Responsible Adults."

The episode explores the gap between digital perception and reality. Ray and Nikhat find themselves caught in a cycle of comparing their "boring" lives to the filtered, high-glamour lives of their peers on Instagram.

The episode follows a high-stakes day for both girls. Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) is trying to climb the corporate ladder and has a critical presentation, while Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) is dealing with the thrill and anxiety of a potential romantic connection. The title reflects the constant "hustle" and the physical and metaphorical state of being "in transit" in life.

The episode is framed around a significant milestone: Nikhat’s (Aisha Ahmed) birthday. While birthdays are usually for celebrating, they often trigger a "Quarter-Life Crisis" where we compare our current reality to the versions of ourselves we imagined "then."

The episode revolves around the nightmare of moving houses in Mumbai. Ray and Nikhat are excited about their new "adult" space, but the transition from the old house to the new one becomes a comedy of errors that tests their patience and their friendship.

The episode explores the "Work-Life Balance" myth. Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed), now in a senior role with a fancy new apartment to pay for, is buried under deadlines, while Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) is trying to figure out how to be a "productive" freelancer without the structure of an office.

The episode centers on the loss of personal space. As Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) spend more time in their new apartment, the "honeymoon phase" of moving in ends. The title reflects the struggle to maintain one’s own identity ("Me") while being part of a co-dependent duo ("Us").

The episode centers on the arrival of Ray’s (Yashaswini Dayama) old school friend. Ray is excited to show off her "cool" Mumbai life, her "cool" roommate Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed), and her "cool" new apartment. However, the reunion doesn't go as planned, leading to a major case of "Social Comparison Anxiety."

Everything that could go wrong, does. The episode is a "comedy of errors" that quickly turns into an emotional crucible. As the girls juggle professional disasters and personal health scares, they are forced to answer the question: Are we just friends because it’s convenient, or are we family?

The episode picks up with Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) feeling the absolute peak of urban exhaustion. Between Nikhat’s soul-crushing corporate deadlines and Ray’s chaotic freelance schedule, they realize they are running on fumes. To blow off some steam before their planned trip home, they decide to have one last "epic" Mumbai night.

The episode follows Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) as they settle into their respective family homes. The initial "pampering phase" (where parents cook your favorite meals and do your laundry) ends abruptly, replaced by the suffocating routine and expectations they once ran away from.

While still in their respective hometowns, Ray (Yashaswini Dayama) and Nikhat (Aisha Ahmed) encounter people from their past. The episode highlights the awkward friction that occurs when you realize your old friends have either stayed exactly the same or changed in ways you can no longer relate to.

The episode explores the complex, multi-generational layers of female relationships. It’s not just about the friendship between the two leads, but about the "sisterhood" they share with their mothers and the realization that their mothers were once young, ambitious, and confused women too.

The title "Out Of Office" is a play on their professional status, but it more accurately reflects their mental state. They’ve been "out of office" from their Mumbai lives for long enough to gain a new perspective. The episode focuses on the inevitable departure and the emotional weight of saying goodbye—this time with the maturity of adults who know exactly what they are going back to.

theme.name: The Lighter Note
theme.shortDescription: Light humour dramas with real taste of the real world around us!
theme.description: Light humour dramas with real taste of the real world around us!

description: Dice Media brings premium Indian web series with relatable stories of modern life—drama, rom-coms, comedy, and workplace tales featuring friendship, careers, and relationships.

title: Filter Copy

schedules.description: It humorously shows how moms unintentionally embarrass their kids by bringing up awkward or personal things. The sketches capture the funny yet relatable moments of such situations.

The video humorously compares typical behaviors of other people with the unique habits and quirks of Marwaris. It highlights cultural traits, spending styles, and funny situations that make the contrast entertaining and relatable.
The video humorously portrays the struggles and quirks of having curly hair. It highlights the funny situations, compliments, and frustrations curly-haired girls experience in daily life.

schedules.programName: When Your Best Friend Gets Married
schedules.description: You’re excited, emotional, jealous, and proud all at once—the shift from daily friendship to occasional calls hits harder than expected.

schedules.programName: Signs You Have The Best Sister
schedules.description: The video shows the sweet and funny moments that prove you have the best sister. It highlights her support, teasing, and unconditional love that make the sibling bond so special.

The video imagines Indian moms with spy-like abilities — covertly listening, gathering info, and being always alert. It highlights the funny extremes of their awareness, intuition, and how nothing gets past them unnoticed.

This compilation video humorously contrasts the behaviors and quirks of dog lovers and cat lovers. The "Cat Lovers" segment features Madhu Gudi with her cat Goldy, showcasing typical cat behaviors like seeking attention, sitting on fans, and the unique bond between a cat and its owner
Your grandmother becomes your confidante, partner-in-crime, and emotional support — blurring generational lines. The video shows the fun, loyalty, and occasional friction in that special bond.

That magical, awkward, life-changing moment when you realize your partner might be “the one” — complete with butterflies, hesitation, overthinking, and emotional confession. The video balances realism with romantic idealism.

The “so what did you study?” “When will you settle down?” “Why aren’t you drinking less?” kind of dad-talk — full of pauses, sighs, and “fine, I’m fine”. The video captures the cringe and charm of talks with dad.
The mood swings, cravings, excitement, panic, and sweet chaos of expecting parents navigating pregnancy together.
Two sisters (or siblings) talk fashion — from borrowing clothes, critiquing style choices, to fighting over accessories. It’s a mix of rivalry, admiration, and shared style secrets.

The video humorously captures the funny, awkward, and sometimes painful thoughts that run through your mind while waxing. It highlights the relatable mix of dread, discomfort, and self-reflection during the process.
The video compares friendships in school/college days with how they are now. It highlights the nostalgia, changes, and the bond that still remains strong.

schedules.programName: When Your Bff Has Another Bff
schedules.description: The shift when your best friend starts spending more time with someone else; the strange mix of feeling replaced, missing your old dynamic, trying not to be jealous while still wanting to hang out with them.
A satirical take on the idea that love for the country now comes with a “certificate” you must constantly prove.

schedules.programName: When Your Partner Loves You But Can't Express It
schedules.description: The video portrays relationships where one partner struggles to express love. It highlights the sweet, awkward, and heartfelt moments of unspoken affection.

schedules.programName: When You Realise Your Younger Sibling Has Grown Up
schedules.description: That surreal shift when your once-tiny sibling starts adulting—and you’re hit by nostalgia and pride.
The video showcases the funny, quirky, and sometimes annoying things brothers typically do. It highlights the playful teasing, mischief, and unique bond shared between bros.

schedules.programName: We All Deserve A Boss Like Him
schedules.description: Here’s the boss who actually gets it: acknowledges your effort, cracks a joke when stress hits, listens when you complain—and makes coming to work less of a drag.

The video imagines a 90s Bollywood-style romance—and shows how it would play out today with modern technology and social norms. It contrasts the dramatic, over-the-top declarations and music of old with how things like texting, social media, and everyday logistics change the romance vibe.

schedules.programName: When You Have A Crush On Your Boss Part 2
schedules.description: The series continues with awkward glances, mis-read messages and “Did they really mean that?!” moments as you try to navigate a crush on your boss in the office. All while pretending you’re just “team-meeting focused.”

schedules.programName: Holi Special: Story Of 4 Single Friends
schedules.description: The video shows four single friends celebrating Holi together. It highlights their fun, playful banter, and how friendship makes festivals special.

After years apart, meeting school friends again brings nostalgia, awkwardness, comparisons (life, looks, careers), and the joy of remembering old stories. The video captures that mix of “I remember you” and “what happened to you.”
The video humorously captures the everyday awkward situations students face in college. It highlights embarrassing encounters, funny slip-ups, and relatable campus moments.

schedules.programName: When Arts Student Falls For Science Student
schedules.description: A charming opposites-attract story that highlights the funny clashes between creativity and logic when an arts student dates a science student.

schedules.programName: Story Of Every Government Exam Student
schedules.description: A young aspirant juggles coaching, hopes and endless revisions while repeating “Next time for sure!” with every attempt. The video captures the roller-coaster of determination, procrastination and exam stress.

schedules.programName: Things Only Girl Best Friends Do
schedules.description: From matching outfits, inside jokes, sister-level honesty, to secret plans and shared playlists — this video showcases how girl best friends operate in their own world. Full of loyalty, giggles and codewords.

schedules.programName: When You're Single And Your Friends Are Dating
schedules.description: The video humorously portrays the dynamics when you're single and your friends are in relationships. It highlights the feeling of being the "third wheel" and the humorous situations that arise from it.

The video portrays the typical experiences and interactions one has when visiting a tailor shop in India. It highlights the common scenarios, misunderstandings, and amusing moments that occur during such visits.
From endless tangles to hair-in-everything problems—a funny look at the pain of long locks.
A funny yet honest portrayal of the nervousness, overthinking, and awkward planning that come with preparing for your “first time.”

This video explores the relatable and often humorous experiences of couples after getting married and the honeymoon phase is over. It highlights the changes in dynamics as they transition from being boyfriend/girlfriend to husband and wife.

schedules.programName: If Doctors Could Hear Your Thoughts
schedules.description: A hilarious peek into what would happen if doctors could hear every anxious, dramatic, or random thought their patients have during check-ups.
Math, Science, English, and History as human personalities—some annoying, some fun, and all too relatable.

schedules.programName: When A Topper Falls In Love With A Backbencher
schedules.description: The academic world collides with romance: one’s always ahead in class, the other’s lagging behind — yet hearts beat anyway. The video shows how opposites in studies find common ground in love.

schedules.programName: 8 Ways Your Partner Drives You Mad
schedules.description: A humorous checklist of those little habits and quirks in your significant other that drive you crazy — from hogging the blanket to weird sleeping positions. All done in relatably exaggerated sketches.

schedules.programName: When You Can't Go Home For Diwali
schedules.description: The video highlights the bittersweet experience of not being able to go home for Diwali, featuring a student who misses her family's celebrations. Despite her initial disappointment, her family surprises her by joining her, making her Diwali special

In a baby’s world: “Why am I small? What’s that giant thing called a toy? Where’s my milk again?” — the video imagines the simple but curious internal tongue of a baby. It’s adorable and funny at the same time.

schedules.programName: When You Are An Only Child
schedules.description: The perks (undivided attention, full bed) and pangs (no sibling backup, solitude) of being an only child — all wrapped in funny, bittersweet moments. It’s a tribute to a life of solo siblinghood.
From obsessing over blending brushes to dramatic contour fails—this one’s for every beauty enthusiast.

schedules.programName: When Your Partner Cheats On You
schedules.description: The emotional roller-coaster of discovering infidelity: the trust shattered, the shock, the confrontation and the difficult decision of what comes next. Heart-break meets self-reflection.

The video humorously contrasts the habits and achievements of “other students” with your own. It highlights the funny struggles, procrastination, and relatable moments of trying to keep up in school or college.

schedules.programName: When A Delhi Boy Falls For A Mumbai Girl
schedules.description: Culture-clash, language mishaps, food-fights and the long-distance jokes: a Delhi boy navigating the Mumbai way of life while falling for a girl who lives it.

The journey of a Chartered Accountant aspirant — sleepless nights, endless revisions, social life sacrificed, and pressure from family & society. It portrays CA life as a tough balancing act between dreams and stress.

schedules.programName: When You Date A Food Lover
schedules.description: Dates revolve around food, arguments over “where to eat,” and the constant temptation to steal bites from your partner’s plate.

The video humorously contrasts idealized, picture-perfect couples with the messy, realistic dynamics of everyday relationships. It highlights the funny, imperfect moments that make love authentic and relatable.
A comedic take on the “perfect” damaad every Indian parent dreams of—respectful, helpful, responsible. But real-life sons-in-law rarely fit this mythical description.

schedules.programName: When You Go Home After A Long Time
schedules.description: The comfort of maa ke haath ka khana, nosy relatives, and the joy of rediscovering your childhood bedroom.

schedules.programName: Middle Class Things We All Do
schedules.description: A nostalgic, humorous take on all the small, quirky habits that define being middle class in India – from rationing electricity to bargaining at every shop. It highlights the shared pride and compromises of a “middle class” lif

schedules.programName: When You Have A Crush On Someone
schedules.description: Every overthinker’s paradise: decoding texts, overanalyzing smiles, and mistaking friendliness for love.

This FilterCopy video humorously captures the chaotic and relatable struggles of exam preparation. Ashish Chanchlani and Viraj showcase every student’s panic, procrastination, and last-minute cramming moments before exams.

schedules.programName: Moving From A Small Town To A Big City

The video captures the bittersweet emotions of the last day of college. It highlights the nostalgia, friendships, and heartfelt goodbyes that make this milestone unforgettable.

schedules.programName: When You Think Everything Is A Sign
schedules.description: You find meaning in random coincidences: the phone rings right when you were thinking of someone, the song you disliked plays, you see an old number—so you start believing the universe is “talking” to you.

From insisting on “just a trim” to miraculously gaining ten inches of hair, this video pokes fun at the clichés every guy goes through at the salon. It captures the disconnect between what men ask for and what they actually get.

schedules.programName: When Your Bff Is Older Than You
schedules.description: The dynamic of having a bestie who’s your mentor, life coach, and chaos partner rolled into one.

A heartfelt and humorous take on school life for the “average” student: not top of the class, not bottom either—just navigating expectations, grades, fun and the invisible stress of staying “good enough”.

schedules.programName: Things Single Women Have To Deal With
schedules.description: The video humorously shows the everyday struggles single women face. It highlights societal questions, unwanted advice, and the funny situations that come with being single.
A relatable take on post-breakup friendship — from emotional support and venting sessions to plotting revenge and ice cream-fueled pep talks.

A heartfelt yet funny look at the quirks, silent sacrifices and the unspoken ways fathers show up — from fixing things to just being there. The video celebrates dads in their unique, often unnoticed style.
From secret treats to bedtime stories and unconditional love, this one’s a warm hug in video form.
A newly-wed bride’s toolkit of witty one-liners and bold responses for those aunties, uncles and relatives. The video plays up the idea of being classy but savage when family dramas hit.
The introvert’s anthem—dodging parties, small talk, and pretending to be busy when someone says “Let’s hang out!”

schedules.programName: Sibling Wars Badi Behen Vs Choti Behen
schedules.description: The older-sister vs younger-sister saga: authority battles, petty fights, secret changing-room bans, and a surprising amount of caring behind the theatrics.

schedules.programName: If You Could Hear Your Crush's Thoughts
schedules.description: This video comically explores the scenarios that unfold if you could hear your crush's thoughts. It highlights the internal monologues, often contrasting with their outward actions, providing a humorous look at the anxieties and desires involved in a crush.

Navigating budgets, guest lists, rituals, outfit choices and mom’s expectations: every exchange becomes a mini-negotiation. The video showcases the wait, the stress, and the sweet chaos of wedding-planning talks with mom.

schedules.programName: If You Worked In Office Like You Work From Home
schedules.description: The video imagines how chaotic and unprofessional it would be if people behaved in an office the same way they do while working from home. It highlights the funny contrasts between remote work habits and real office etiquette.

schedules.programName: Filtercopy | Nani Ka Ghar | नानी का घर
schedules.description: A warm nostalgic trip to Grandma’s house—endless food, pampering, cousins, and that special comfort you can’t find anywhere else.

schedules.programName: When Your Best Friend Leaves Office
schedules.description: When your office buddy moves on: the swap from daily gossip sessions and lunch-huddles to suddenly being solo, and the quiet realisation of how much they held up your workday.
The shift from “I’ll be productive” optimism to pajama-all-day acceptance—lockdown fatigue captured hilariously.

schedules.programName: When Your Bff Is A Lifesaver
schedules.description: When your best friend swoops in exactly when you need them: the back-up plan for when everything else fails, the one who holds the umbrella when you forgot yours.
The video humorously shows the excitement and chaos of celebrating Holi with friends. It highlights playful moments, colors, and the spirit of togetherness.

From obsessive checking of notifications, posting for the ‘gram, to weird internal monologues while scrolling—this video holds a mirror to all the ridiculous (and somehow relatable) digital quirks we’ve got.
It humorously shows how moms unintentionally embarrass their kids by bringing up awkward or personal things. The sketches capture the funny yet relatable moments of such situations.

The video humorously compares typical behaviors of other people with the unique habits and quirks of Marwaris. It highlights cultural traits, spending styles, and funny situations that make the contrast entertaining and relatable.
The video humorously portrays the struggles and quirks of having curly hair. It highlights the funny situations, compliments, and frustrations curly-haired girls experience in daily life.

schedules.programName: When Your Best Friend Gets Married
schedules.description: You’re excited, emotional, jealous, and proud all at once—the shift from daily friendship to occasional calls hits harder than expected.

schedules.programName: Signs You Have The Best Sister
schedules.description: The video shows the sweet and funny moments that prove you have the best sister. It highlights her support, teasing, and unconditional love that make the sibling bond so special.

The video imagines Indian moms with spy-like abilities — covertly listening, gathering info, and being always alert. It highlights the funny extremes of their awareness, intuition, and how nothing gets past them unnoticed.

This compilation video humorously contrasts the behaviors and quirks of dog lovers and cat lovers. The "Cat Lovers" segment features Madhu Gudi with her cat Goldy, showcasing typical cat behaviors like seeking attention, sitting on fans, and the unique bond between a cat and its owner
Your grandmother becomes your confidante, partner-in-crime, and emotional support — blurring generational lines. The video shows the fun, loyalty, and occasional friction in that special bond.

That magical, awkward, life-changing moment when you realize your partner might be “the one” — complete with butterflies, hesitation, overthinking, and emotional confession. The video balances realism with romantic idealism.

The “so what did you study?” “When will you settle down?” “Why aren’t you drinking less?” kind of dad-talk — full of pauses, sighs, and “fine, I’m fine”. The video captures the cringe and charm of talks with dad.
The mood swings, cravings, excitement, panic, and sweet chaos of expecting parents navigating pregnancy together.
Two sisters (or siblings) talk fashion — from borrowing clothes, critiquing style choices, to fighting over accessories. It’s a mix of rivalry, admiration, and shared style secrets.

The video humorously captures the funny, awkward, and sometimes painful thoughts that run through your mind while waxing. It highlights the relatable mix of dread, discomfort, and self-reflection during the process.
The video compares friendships in school/college days with how they are now. It highlights the nostalgia, changes, and the bond that still remains strong.

schedules.programName: When Your Bff Has Another Bff
schedules.description: The shift when your best friend starts spending more time with someone else; the strange mix of feeling replaced, missing your old dynamic, trying not to be jealous while still wanting to hang out with them.
A satirical take on the idea that love for the country now comes with a “certificate” you must constantly prove.

schedules.programName: When Your Partner Loves You But Can't Express It
schedules.description: The video portrays relationships where one partner struggles to express love. It highlights the sweet, awkward, and heartfelt moments of unspoken affection.

schedules.programName: When You Realise Your Younger Sibling Has Grown Up
schedules.description: That surreal shift when your once-tiny sibling starts adulting—and you’re hit by nostalgia and pride.
The video showcases the funny, quirky, and sometimes annoying things brothers typically do. It highlights the playful teasing, mischief, and unique bond shared between bros.

schedules.programName: We All Deserve A Boss Like Him
schedules.description: Here’s the boss who actually gets it: acknowledges your effort, cracks a joke when stress hits, listens when you complain—and makes coming to work less of a drag.

The video imagines a 90s Bollywood-style romance—and shows how it would play out today with modern technology and social norms. It contrasts the dramatic, over-the-top declarations and music of old with how things like texting, social media, and everyday logistics change the romance vibe.

schedules.programName: When You Have A Crush On Your Boss Part 2
schedules.description: The series continues with awkward glances, mis-read messages and “Did they really mean that?!” moments as you try to navigate a crush on your boss in the office. All while pretending you’re just “team-meeting focused.”

schedules.programName: Holi Special: Story Of 4 Single Friends
schedules.description: The video shows four single friends celebrating Holi together. It highlights their fun, playful banter, and how friendship makes festivals special.

After years apart, meeting school friends again brings nostalgia, awkwardness, comparisons (life, looks, careers), and the joy of remembering old stories. The video captures that mix of “I remember you” and “what happened to you.”
The video humorously captures the everyday awkward situations students face in college. It highlights embarrassing encounters, funny slip-ups, and relatable campus moments.

schedules.programName: When Arts Student Falls For Science Student
schedules.description: A charming opposites-attract story that highlights the funny clashes between creativity and logic when an arts student dates a science student.

schedules.programName: Story Of Every Government Exam Student
schedules.description: A young aspirant juggles coaching, hopes and endless revisions while repeating “Next time for sure!” with every attempt. The video captures the roller-coaster of determination, procrastination and exam stress.

schedules.programName: Things Only Girl Best Friends Do
schedules.description: From matching outfits, inside jokes, sister-level honesty, to secret plans and shared playlists — this video showcases how girl best friends operate in their own world. Full of loyalty, giggles and codewords.

schedules.programName: When You're Single And Your Friends Are Dating
schedules.description: The video humorously portrays the dynamics when you're single and your friends are in relationships. It highlights the feeling of being the "third wheel" and the humorous situations that arise from it.

The video portrays the typical experiences and interactions one has when visiting a tailor shop in India. It highlights the common scenarios, misunderstandings, and amusing moments that occur during such visits.
From endless tangles to hair-in-everything problems—a funny look at the pain of long locks.
A funny yet honest portrayal of the nervousness, overthinking, and awkward planning that come with preparing for your “first time.”

This video explores the relatable and often humorous experiences of couples after getting married and the honeymoon phase is over. It highlights the changes in dynamics as they transition from being boyfriend/girlfriend to husband and wife.

schedules.programName: If Doctors Could Hear Your Thoughts
schedules.description: A hilarious peek into what would happen if doctors could hear every anxious, dramatic, or random thought their patients have during check-ups.
Math, Science, English, and History as human personalities—some annoying, some fun, and all too relatable.

schedules.programName: When A Topper Falls In Love With A Backbencher
schedules.description: The academic world collides with romance: one’s always ahead in class, the other’s lagging behind — yet hearts beat anyway. The video shows how opposites in studies find common ground in love.

schedules.programName: 8 Ways Your Partner Drives You Mad
schedules.description: A humorous checklist of those little habits and quirks in your significant other that drive you crazy — from hogging the blanket to weird sleeping positions. All done in relatably exaggerated sketches.

schedules.programName: When You Can't Go Home For Diwali
schedules.description: The video highlights the bittersweet experience of not being able to go home for Diwali, featuring a student who misses her family's celebrations. Despite her initial disappointment, her family surprises her by joining her, making her Diwali special

In a baby’s world: “Why am I small? What’s that giant thing called a toy? Where’s my milk again?” — the video imagines the simple but curious internal tongue of a baby. It’s adorable and funny at the same time.

schedules.programName: When You Are An Only Child
schedules.description: The perks (undivided attention, full bed) and pangs (no sibling backup, solitude) of being an only child — all wrapped in funny, bittersweet moments. It’s a tribute to a life of solo siblinghood.
From obsessing over blending brushes to dramatic contour fails—this one’s for every beauty enthusiast.

schedules.programName: When Your Partner Cheats On You
schedules.description: The emotional roller-coaster of discovering infidelity: the trust shattered, the shock, the confrontation and the difficult decision of what comes next. Heart-break meets self-reflection.

The video humorously contrasts the habits and achievements of “other students” with your own. It highlights the funny struggles, procrastination, and relatable moments of trying to keep up in school or college.

schedules.programName: When A Delhi Boy Falls For A Mumbai Girl
schedules.description: Culture-clash, language mishaps, food-fights and the long-distance jokes: a Delhi boy navigating the Mumbai way of life while falling for a girl who lives it.

The journey of a Chartered Accountant aspirant — sleepless nights, endless revisions, social life sacrificed, and pressure from family & society. It portrays CA life as a tough balancing act between dreams and stress.

schedules.programName: When You Date A Food Lover
schedules.description: Dates revolve around food, arguments over “where to eat,” and the constant temptation to steal bites from your partner’s plate.

The video humorously contrasts idealized, picture-perfect couples with the messy, realistic dynamics of everyday relationships. It highlights the funny, imperfect moments that make love authentic and relatable.
A comedic take on the “perfect” damaad every Indian parent dreams of—respectful, helpful, responsible. But real-life sons-in-law rarely fit this mythical description.

schedules.programName: When You Go Home After A Long Time
schedules.description: The comfort of maa ke haath ka khana, nosy relatives, and the joy of rediscovering your childhood bedroom.

schedules.programName: Middle Class Things We All Do
schedules.description: A nostalgic, humorous take on all the small, quirky habits that define being middle class in India – from rationing electricity to bargaining at every shop. It highlights the shared pride and compromises of a “middle class” lif

schedules.programName: When You Have A Crush On Someone
schedules.description: Every overthinker’s paradise: decoding texts, overanalyzing smiles, and mistaking friendliness for love.

This FilterCopy video humorously captures the chaotic and relatable struggles of exam preparation. Ashish Chanchlani and Viraj showcase every student’s panic, procrastination, and last-minute cramming moments before exams.

schedules.programName: Moving From A Small Town To A Big City
schedules.description: A heartfelt story about chasing dreams, culture shock, loneliness, and finally finding your place in the chaos.

schedules.programName: If Your Life Were A Rajinikanth Movie
schedules.description: Over-the-top drama, slow-mo entries, and impossible stunts—because life would be so much cooler with Rajini-style swag.
The video captures the chaos and excitement of school lunch breaks. It highlights the rush, the friendships, and the small adventures that make those moments memorable.

schedules.programName: When Your Partner Is Annoying But Cute
schedules.description: The video shows all the little annoying things partners do that can drive you crazy. Yet, it highlights how those same quirks make them irresistibly cute and lovable.

theme.name: Emotions
theme.shortDescription: The reel lives embracing the real life emotions and making everyone feel connected!
theme.description: The reel lives embracing the real life emotions and making everyone feel connected!

description: FilterCopy brings you fun, relatable videos on real-life moments — from family drama and office chaos to dating and more — turning everyday struggles into pure laughter.

schedules.programName: Shahenshah Of Bollywood-83rd Birthday Special Vol 2
schedules.description: Iconic melodies of Amitabh Bachchan reflecting romance,pride, and cinematic brilliance.
Dive into the emotions of life, with a collection of heartfelt songs that beautifully capture the highs and lows of life. Let these timeless tunes resonate with your emotions and experiences.

schedules.programName: Dilip Kumar – Tributes To A Legend
schedules.description: Celebrate the voice of a generation with songs immortalized by the charisma of Dilip Kumar. Soul-stirring ghazals, patriotic numbers, and emotional ballads that reflect a cinematic titan’s journey.
Feel-good songs to groove to. Perfect for boosting your mood and adding fun to any moment – pure, carefree energy!
Soothing melodies that calm your soul. Let these peaceful tunes create your perfect moment of serenity. A carefully curated collection of rhythms to help you unwind.
Bring back the flashy disco vibes with this sensational Disco Dancer jukebox. Whether you're a retro lover or a new-age dancer, these beats will keep you moving!
Relive the golden era of music with classic melodies, retro rhythms, and timeless tunes that never fade. A nostalgic trip for true old-school lovers!
Fall in love all over again with Kumar Sanu & Alka Yagnik! Their magical duets—full of passion, heartbreak, and nostalgia—are pure 90s gold.

A powerhouse collection of R.D. Burman's iconic hits, blending innovation, emotion, and energy. From soulful ballads to electrifying grooves, experience the genius of Pancham Da that defined Bollywood's golden soundscape.
Step into Bollywood’s most soulful decade with this jukebox of evergreen melodies. A rich tapestry of romance, innocence, and timeless charm – pure nostalgia from the golden 70s.
Take a ride through the vibrant 90s with peppy love anthems, dramatic duets, and emotional melodies. This jukebox celebrates the signature style of Bollywood's musical revival decade.
Revisit the unmatched charm of Rajesh Khanna with this jukebox of unforgettable melodies. Romantic, philosophical, and heartfelt – these songs defined an era and a superstar.
Dive into Jeetendra’s iconic hits—The Jumping Jack’s timeless energy! Relive the magic of Bollywood’s golden era with foot-tapping beats, romance, and pure nostalgia!
Turn up the retro vibes with Neetu Singh’s greatest hits! A birthday playlist packed with nostalgia, romance, and endless charm.
Relive the '90s with Superhits! Romantic melodies, peppy beats, and timeless nostalgia—dance, sing along, and fall in love all over again!
Time-travel through Dharmendra's iconic hits – the ultimate He-Man of Bollywood! Timeless romance, unforgettable melodies that define an era of pure masala magic!
Press play on nostalgia! Alka Yagnik's velvet voice brings back memories with these evergreen hits that still give us goosebumps today.
Dance through the disco era with Dimple & Neetu! Playful whispers, foot-tapping romance, and melodies that defined a generation’s dreams.
Get ready to groove with Mithun Da's greatest hits! From 'Disco Dancer' to romantic ballads, this collection is pure Bollywood retro gold.
Dive into these timeless tracks that shaped Hindi cinema's musical heritage. The golden touch of B.R. Chopra - where every song became legendary.
